description.narrative: Insatsen är en plan för policy dialog och kapacitetsutveckling för ukrainska myndigheter. Baserat på erfarenhet, pågående projekt och den ukrainska reform agendan har följande fem pelare valts ut: - Investeringsklimat – stöd till anti-korruptionsreformagendan är i fokus - Banksektorn – stöd för stabilisering av banksektorn och utveckling av kapitalmarknader - Energi – stöd till omstrukturering av statligt ägda företag och stöd till utarbetande och implementering av regelverk - Företagssektorn – ökad konkurrenskraft, utökning av handel och tillgång till krediter - Infrastruktur – stöd till institutionell kapacitet

The proposal from the EBRD, “EBRD-Ukraine Stabilisation and Sustainable Growth Multi-Donor Account (MDA)” has been developed in the light of the economic crisis that emerged as a result of the political conflict and the ensuing military conflict in the eastern part of Ukraine. This is an operational response to the new needs and transition opportunities and addresses the urgent needs as regards support for the design and implementation of policy reforms and institutional capacity building as well as investment support, all in agreement with the Ukrainian government and other public authorities. The programme offers short hand medium -term technical cooperation (TC), mostly consisting of policy dialogue and institutional capacity building, to different Ukrainian authorities.
Based on an appraisal of EBRD´s strengths, the Ukrainian priority agenda as well as the current donor setting including actors such as the World Bank, IMF and other International Financial Institutions (IFIs), the proposal focuses on the following pillars, with examples associated overall sectoral objectives and activities:
- Investment climate – where support to the anti-corruption reform agenda is particularly important - Banking sector – support to the stabilization of the banking sector and development of capital and money markets - Energy – support to the restructuring of state owned enterprises and support to the drafting and implementation of enabling legislative and regulatory frameworks - Corporate sector – increased competitiveness, expansion of trade and increased access to finance - Infrastructure – strengthen institutional capacity and support liberalization, assisting the implementation of transport reforms

"1.01 Purpose of cooperation funds: The Activities shall focus on stabilising Ukraine's macroeconomic situation and fostering Ukraine's growth rebound."
Under agreement objective stated in clause 1.01, the Multi Donor Account (EBRD) will address the country's urgent needs as regards support for the design and implementation of policy reforms and institutional capacity building in agreement with the Government and other public authorities of Ukraine as well as investment support. The identified needs are at the core of stabilizing Ukraine's macroeconomic situation in the short run and will also seek to foster Ukraine's growth rebound in the medium-to-longer term.

title.narrative: Decision on contribution amendment EBRD Ukraine 2019

description.narrative:
Progress during 2022 and result examples from the 2021-2022 report include the following: 2022
- 21 projects have been paused during 2022, but others have continued. So far (to October), 11 new projects have been approved with a project value of approximately €9.1 million.
- €8 million has been allocated to Ukraine Reform Architecture (URA) programme, which represent the most significant programme in terms of progress during the year. URA has been a focal vehicle for technical assistance to Government agencies during the war, which adapted to meet the resilience and recovery needs of the Ukrainian Government. Specific support has been provided to the logistics of humanitarian efforts, the wartime economy and the countrys EU accession efforts.
URA supported the establishment and launch of 23 working groups on the preparation of the Recovery Plan (URA consultants coordinate all working groups except defense and security) support to the preparation of the Ukraine Recovery Conference 2022 (URC) in Lugano Development and launch of the Humanitarian Aid platform.
- Successful launch and organisation of work of the sectoral working group Functioning of the Financial System and preparation of proposals for constituent documents of the working subgroups.
- Design support to the visualisation of Recovery Plan. Ministry of Finance Activities in the context of international experience. Analysis of best practices in the area of reconstruction and modernization of war-torn economies. Provision of support to the Ministry with analytics of healthcare systems financial indicators. Participation in the working groups "Functioning of the Financial System", "Renewal and Development of Infrastructure", "Veteran Protection and Social Protection of Citizens" and preparation of recommendations for the Recovery Plan.
- Provision of support for the President's Office with preparation of daily speeches and communication materials.
- Support for development of tax and customs incentives to simplify the requirements for businesses and speed up procedures during the war. Data collection and analytical support to the evaluation of damages in buildings and infrastructure objects. Provision of sectoral analytical inputs to the EU accession Questionnaire.
- Support provided for the alignment of Ukraines framework for confidentiality and professional secrecy with EU standards
- Support provided for EBRD Clients in addressing Gender-Based Violence issues in Conflict-Affected Ukraine
2021-2022 achievements aggregated
Public administration (20 projects) 1) The Ukrainian Parliament passed the law on Bondholders Representatives in June 2020 2) Five new laws and one secondary legislation adopted as part of URA project 3) Single portal for civil service vacancies for all ministries completed and launched under URA project 4) Deposit Guarantee Fund restructuring scenario approved by the Financial Stability Council 5) Diagnostic study of capacity of Ministry of Infrastructure delivered and recommendations accepted
Corporate governance (8 projects) 1) The Ukrainian Corporate Governance Academy provided 5 events and 4 webinars for UNIC members on policy and compliance during Business Integrity Month
Public private dialogue (6 projects) 1) 650 recommendations issued by Business Ombudsman Initiative (BOI), 89% implemented 2) 4 recommendations on investment climate improvements issued by the National Investment Council, of which 3 were implemented (2 new laws were adopted) and 1 is in progress 3) Action Plan for reforming the framework for implementation of sovereign and sub-sovereign investment projects financed by IFIs presented to Government
Competitiveness (10 projects) 1) Eight assignments initiated supporting investment projects under the Ukraine Public Transport Investment Framework. 2) Client Naftogaz formally announced their commitment to report on emissions (UN standard), the first EBRD client to do so 3) Capacity building completed to OschadBank on risk management, micro-lending and SME lending capacity building and streamlining of the debt collection system
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
